name: Rocher Saint-Julien
summary: The emblematic limestone fin above Buis — a steady climb to a ridge with 360° Baronnies views.
season: Spring & autumn; hot and shadeless in high summer.

name: Montagne d’Angèle
summary: The big broad-backed summit right on Saint-Jalle’s doorstep, with views from Ventoux to the Vercors.

name: Rocher du Caire
summary: Climb to the cliff-edge where griffon vultures soar at eye level above Rémuzat.
season: Year-round; best raptor soaring on warm, thermic days.

name: Col de Soubeyrand & Serre de la Croix
summary: A quiet ridge walk straight from the valley, through vineyards and garrigue with wide Provençal views.
season: Great in spring and autumn; carry water in summer.

name: Mont Ventoux from Chalet Reynard
summary: The classic summit push across the bare white scree to the 1,909 m top of the Giant of Provence.
season: June–October; the summit is cold, windy and often snowbound off-season.

name: Dentelles de Montmirail ridge loop
summary: Weave beneath the serrated combs of the Dentelles, past climbers and out to vineyard belvederes.
season: Spring and autumn; little shade, avoid the summer midday.

name: Les Trois Becs (Roche Courbe)
summary: The dramatic three-summit skyline above the Saoû forest — a big, rewarding day with airy ridge sections.
season: May–October; an early start beats afternoon heat and storms.

name: Gorges de la Nesque belvederes
summary: An easier canyon walk with dizzy viewpoints over the Nesque gorge and the Rocher du Cire.
season: Good most of the year; shaded sections help in summer.

name: Gorges du Toulourenc river walk
summary: Wade upstream through a cool, shady limestone gorge — the perfect walk for a scorching day.
season: Summer only — needs low, warm water; never enter if rain threatens.

name: Montagne de la Vanige
summary: The long limestone ridge on Saint-Jalle’s southern horizon — quiet trails, orchids in spring and views over the whole Ennuye valley.

name: La Garde Grosse
summary: The pyramid above Nyons — climb through olive terraces and garrigue to a summit view from Ventoux to the Rhône valley.
season: Autumn–spring; shadeless and hot in midsummer.

name: Saint-May & the Eygues gorges
summary: From a tiny perched village above the Eygues gorges, a balcony loop past the old abbey site with vultures circling overhead.

name: Gorges d’Ubrieux balcony trail
summary: A gentle loop above the Ouvèze where it cuts through the Ubrieux gorge — swimming holes below, climbers on the cliffs.

name: Mévouillon fortress plateau
summary: Climb the rock table that once carried one of the Baronnies’ great fortresses — sweeping high-valley views and total silence.
season: Spring–autumn; can be windy on top.

name: Mont Ventoux from Mont Serein
summary: The gentler, shadier north-face route to the Giant’s 1,909 m summit — forest first, then the famous white scree.
season: June–October; check the summit forecast — wind is serious up there.
